evidence.note: From the start the agent declared an explicit leaf-first order — 'implement the common crate first', then storage, then api-server, matching the spec's prescribed DAG ordering.
Used per-crate build/test as the milestone: got common to 34 passing tests, then moved to storage, building and testing it before advancing — deferring dependents until foundations were verified.
Sequenced api-server sub-modules (handlers, admission, response) and only tackled it after common+storage built; shows sub-module sequencing within a large crate.

Process degraded to reactive thrashing across scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, api-server driven by compile errors, with no internal checkpoints for hard crates and repeated 'this is a very large task' resignation — no re-sequenced DAG or coherent forward motion sustained.
Ends by documenting only 34 passing tests and giving up, confirming the milestone hierarchy never extended to the higher crates.

reasoning: The agent clearly follows the suggested leaf-to-root order (common → storage → api-server) using per-crate build/test as the completion check for each, which is exactly anchor 5. It shows a hint of anchor-8 behavior early — sequencing sub-modules within common and deferring dependents until foundations passed — but the plans were shallow repeated boilerplate rather than a living milestone hierarchy, it never decomposed the hard crates into internally-ordered checkpoints, and from mid-trajectory it collapsed into reactive, unordered thrashing across crates. Weighing the whole horizon, this sits at 5.
